title: Minimax theorem for a sampled finite game
statement:
Let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function, and let $x : [M] \to \bbr$ and $y : [N] \to \bbr$ be finite families of row and column points such that $0 \le f(x_i, y_j) \le 1$ for all $i$ and $j$. Suppose the column action set is nonempty ($N \ge 1$) and there are at least two row actions ($M \ge 2$). Then the sampled game — the $M \times N$ matrix game with entries $f(x_i, y_j)$ — has equal lower and upper values,
\[
  \sup_{p \in \Delta_M}\; \inf_{j \in [N]}\; \sum_{i} p_i\, f(x_i, y_j)
  \;=\;
  \inf_{q \in \Delta_N}\; \sup_{i \in [M]}\; \sum_{j} f(x_i, y_j)\, q_j,
\]
where $\Delta_M$ and $\Delta_N$ denote the sets of mixed strategies over the row and column actions.
hypotheses_covered: at least one column action (N ≥ 1, NeZero N)
at least one row action (NeZero M)
at least two row actions (1 < M)
replaced:
Under the same size hypotheses as \texttt{OnlineLearning.finite\_minimax\_value},
the sampled game satisfies $v^-(\mathrm{sampledGame}) = v^+(\mathrm{sampledGame})$.
